answer: Agent economies resist Sybil attacks with a bonded identity: an agent locks a stake to get a signing key for one canonical address, and a second identity requires a fresh bond, so N agents cost N stakes. Each registration also pays a fee and must send a heartbeat, a signal of liveness, so idle clones bleed funds. Detection links clusters via shared funding, slashing every sibling once one cheats. The attacker's bill is the entire bond, lost irreversibly per slash, against a tiny vote reward. Each echo or ripple of duplicates becomes visible in the ledger and is priced out.
